ai_root_cause: PC0 has an incorrect default gateway IP address configured, preventing it from forwarding traffic destined for remote networks to the local router.
ai_fix: Access PC0's IP configuration settings. | Update the default gateway address on PC0 from its current incorrect value to 192.168.10.1.
ai_evidence: PC0: ipconfig shows 192.168.10.10, but its default gateway is configured incorrectly. | Router0: show ip interface brief confirms 192.168.10.1 is the gateway for the 192.168.10.0/24 network.

ai_root_cause: PC0 and PC1 are in different VLANs, preventing direct Layer 2 communication.
ai_fix: Configure interface Fa0/2 on Switch0 to be in VLAN 10, or configure Fa0/1 to be in VLAN 20, so both PCs are in the same VLAN. | Alternatively, if inter-VLAN communication is intended, ensure a router is configured for inter-VLAN routing and both PCs have the correct default gateway.
ai_evidence: Switch0: Fa0/1 (PC0) is in VLAN 10 | Switch0: Fa0/2 (likely PC1) is in VLAN 20 | PC0 ping to 192.168.10.11 shows 100% packet loss

ai_root_cause: The router (gateway) is unable to resolve the Layer 2 address (MAC) of the destination server (192.168.20.10) on its local GigabitEthernet0/1 segment via ARP. Because the router cannot map the IP address to a MAC address to encapsulate the frame, it returns a 'Destination host unreachable' error to the source.
ai_fix: Verify the physical cabling or Layer 2 switch connectivity between Router0's GigabitEthernet0/1 and Server0. | Check if Server0 is powered on, configured with the correct IP address (192.168.20.10), and placed in the correct VLAN that corresponds to the network attached to GigabitEthernet0/1. | Ensure that there are no firewalls on Server0 or intermediate Layer 2 devices blocking ARP or ICMP traffic.
ai_evidence: PC0 can reach its gateway (192.168.10.1). | Ping to 192.168.20.10 from PC0 results in 'Destination host unreachable' from 192.168.10.1. | Router0 has 192.168.20.0/24 directly connected on GigabitEthernet0/1. | Interface GigabitEthernet0/1 is up/up. | The error message 'Destination host unreachable' at the Layer 3 boundary (the gateway) indicates the router lacks an ARP entry for the destination IP and cannot resolve it via ARP requests on the connected segment.

ai_root_cause: The PC2 default gateway is incorrectly configured to 10.0.0.1, which is outside its local subnet (192.168.30.0/24), preventing it from routing traffic to any remote network.
ai_fix: Update the Default Gateway setting on PC2 to 192.168.30.1.
ai_evidence: PC2 IP: 192.168.30.15/24 | PC2 Default Gateway: 10.0.0.1 (incorrect) | Router interface for local subnet (Gi0/0): 192.168.30.1

ai_root_cause: An inbound access control list (ACL 100) applied to the router interface is explicitly denying IP traffic from the PC3 subnet destined for the 192.168.40.0/24 server subnet.
ai_fix: Modify access-list 100 on the router to permit traffic from the PC3 subnet to 192.168.40.0/24 (e.g., 'permit ip 192.168.50.0 0.0.0.255 192.168.40.0 0.0.0.255').
ai_evidence: PC3 can reach local gateway 192.168.50.2. | Router routing table shows a valid route for 192.168.40.0/24. | Running-config reveals 'access-group 100 in' applied to the incoming interface for PC3, and 'access-list 100 deny ip any 192.168.40.0 0.0.0.255' explicitly blocking traffic to the server subnet.

ai_root_cause: PC5 has an incorrect default gateway address configured.
ai_fix: Change the default gateway configuration on PC5 to 192.168.60.1.
ai_evidence: PC5 IP configuration shows a default gateway of 192.168.60.10, which is the IP address of PC4, not the router interface 192.168.60.1. | PC4 IP configuration shows correct default gateway of 192.168.60.1. | Router3 shows GigabitEthernet0/0 is 192.168.60.1/24.
